summary:
Our project is a small interactive exhibit about NASA equipment that was sent to space and never came back. It has six colored buttons, and each one plays a short video about a different mission.
We built it using an Arduino. The buttons are connected to the Arduino, which plays the right story when a button is pressed. We started with a cardboard prototype to test the buttons, then designed a themed box around it so it looks like a real museum piece.
Most people know the astronauts, but not the rovers and instruments that worked for years and were then left behind. We wanted visitors, especially kids, to press a button and hear the story of each one. The exhibit works without internet, so it can be used easily in schools and science centers.
details:
Our project for the Space Exploration Interactive Museum challenge is a small exhibit with six colored buttons. Each button is linked to a different NASA mission whose equipment was left in space. When a visitor presses a button, the Arduino reads it and plays the story of that mission.
We built it with an Arduino Nano, six push buttons with colored caps, a breadboard, resistors, jumper wires and a Bluetooth module. After testing the circuit, we put everything inside a box decorated with a space theme so it looks like a real museum piece.
Most people know the astronauts but not the rovers and instruments that worked for years and were then left behind. We wanted kids to press a button and hear the story of each one, so learning feels more like playing a game.
We kept the cost low and made it easy to use for any age. It also works without internet, so it can be used in schools and science centers.
